body:
WHAT
The renderer page sets a Content Security Policy of `default-src 'none'` and allows styles, scripts and fonts only from 'self' (plus img-src 'self' data:). Nothing is loaded from the internet at runtime, so the UI works offline and air-gapped. Both bundled fonts (Inter, JetBrains Mono) are SIL OFL 1.1 and ship with the licence text in app/renderer/fonts/.

WHY
A CDN script, style or font would break the app offline and add a third-party dependency the strict CSP would have to be relaxed for.

WHERE
app/renderer/index.html — <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'none'; style-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self';">, the <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css"> and the relative <script src="modules/*.js"> list. app/renderer/fonts/ — inter-var.woff2, inter-var-italic.woff2, jetbrains-mono-var.woff2, OFL-1.1.txt, README.md. app/scripts/bundle-engine.js copies renderer/fonts into the packaged app.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. The CSP meta tag in index.html contains default-src 'none', style-src 'self', script-src 'self' and font-src 'self', and contains no http:, https: or 'unsafe-inline' source.
2. Every <script src>, <link href> and CSS url(...) in index.html and styles.css is a relative path — none starts with http://, https:// or //.
3. app/renderer/fonts contains OFL-1.1.txt alongside every .woff2 file referenced by styles.css @font-face rules.
4. Loading the renderer in a smoke run with network access blocked produces no CSP violation or failed-resource console error in the log.
5. The packaged build-resources/app/renderer/fonts directory contains the same font files and licence as the source tree.
